title: Potato, baked, peel not eaten, with butter

content.title: About
content.content: Baked potato with the peel removed and served with butter is a popular side dish in many cuisines worldwide. Baking retains most of the potato's nutrients, and the added butter enhances flavor while improving the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Baking caramelizes the natural sugars in potatoes, intensifying their aroma.
Potato skins contain more fiber and vitamins, but they are discarded in this preparation.
Serving baked potatoes with butter is a tradition in Russian, German, and American kitchens.
Potatoes are one of the most consumed root vegetables globally, with annual production exceeding 350 million tonnes.

items.title: Rich source of potassium
items.content: Baked potatoes are high in potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Although some vitamin C is lost during cooking, baked potatoes still provide a notable amount of this antioxidant.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes supply slowly digestible carbs that provide sustained energy and satiety.

items.title: Fat‑soluble vitamins with butter
items.content: Adding butter helps the body absorb vitamins A, D, E, and K present in small amounts in the potato.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Even without the skin, the flesh contains dietary fiber that supports digestive health.

items.title: High calorie content with excess butter
items.content: Using too much butter can increase the dish's calorie density and contribute to weight gain.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Baked potatoes have a high glycemic index, which may cause rapid blood sugar spikes in people with diabetes.

items.title: Butter allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to the type of oil or butter used in preparation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the baked potato hot, drizzled with butter or melted butter. It can be added to salads, used as a base for casseroles, or enjoyed simply as a side dish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked baked potatoes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. Reheat in the oven or microwave to retain a pleasant texture.
